scope: Pure immutable DATA decode reuse feasibility in an existing operation-scoped parser cache; source qualification only.

input.additional_input: one explicitly labelled assembly field excerpt plus scope/ownership facts
input.outside_initial_prefix: full Writer/native internals and later concrete Root wiring; no retroactive source completeness claim

review.implementation_design: rejected whole negative conclusion: confused the requested immutable driver-envelope Complete with a different assembled-observation Complete, then incorrectly concluded every reuse must cache the entire observation and skip fresh IO.
review.independent_audit: partial source observations only: invented IO call edges, proposed locator-only keys, misstated current scope fields, and suggested changing legacy mocks rather than preserving old dispatch.
review.owner_boundary: Concrete caller source proves an ordinary operation parser-cache scope; it does not prove an optional historical filesystem lease is always active. Fully decoded immutable driver DATA has a possible seam after fresh reads, but the new issuer/wiring API is not implemented or qualified.

reusable_rules: Resolve the fully qualified nominal result type before reasoning about its fields, immutability or whether it is forbidden to cache; same simple names are not interchangeable.
A false whole-result-cache negative does not rule out reuse of one pure decode at its original point while every read and contextual validation still occurs.
An operation ThreadLocal parser cache and a filesystem historical lease can coexist but are different lifetimes and authorities; prove each actual entry instead of inferring one from the other.

A new interface default method may reach existing dynamic Proxies as an unknown invocation. Preserve legacy call paths and require explicit concrete opt-in; do not fix compatibility by weakening old tests.
A source-feasible pure-data seam is not an implementation, software pass, deployment or performance result.

cost.marker_basis: original phase-file filesystem mtime; no embedded stopwatch timestamp

limits: No new JVM, test, host, application reload or business action.
No production patch or new API adopted.
No raw source/request/answer, private path, machine/process identity, filename/FQN or application-specific records are public.
